art.subject: White Wagtail of the subspecies Motacilla alba ocularis (East Siberian Wagtail), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on spring migration in Korea in April and May: white forehead and face crossed by a black eye-stripe from the lores through the eye to the ear-coverts; black crown and nape; plain grey mantle, back and rump; a small white patch on the chin, the rest of the throat, foreneck and upper breast black, forming a large bib; belly and undertail white, flanks washed grey; wing coverts blackish with white edges forming two wing-bars, flight feathers dark without a large white panel; long black tail with white outer tail feathers. Thin black bill; dark eye; black legs.
art.pose: walking along the shoreline, side view
art.scene: Korean spring migration: sandy river mouth opening onto the sea; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding (spring), side view standing on sand: white face with black eye-stripe, black crown and nape, grey back, small white chin patch, black throat, foreneck and upper breast, white belly, dark wing with two white wing-bars, black legs

adult winter (autumn and winter), side view standing: white face with black eye-stripe, white chin and throat, black crescent-shaped band across the breast, grey back, white underparts, dark wing with white wing-bars
adult male, folded wing detail in side view: blackish wing coverts with white tips forming two wing-bars, secondaries dark brown to black on the outer webs with no white panel
art.build: Slim, long-tailed wagtail, longer than a sparrow, with a small rounded head, short neck and horizontal stance; walks briskly on sand and mud, pumping its tail up and down. Bill thin, straight and black, a little shorter than the head. Legs fairly long and black. Tail long, narrow and square-ended, black with white outer feathers. Flight deeply undulating; from above the wing shows two white wing-bars on a dark wing rather than a large white panel.
avoid: Do not omit the black eye-stripe; a plain white face without it is Amur Wagtail (Motacilla alba leucopsis).
Do not paint a black back or a largely white wing; those mark Black-backed Wagtail (Motacilla alba lugens).
Do not paint any yellow in the plumage, or pink legs.
Do not give winter birds a fully black throat; in winter the throat is white and only a black breast band remains.
